hints: A suffix automaton compactly represents all substrings.
Each transition appends a character; paths from the initial state represent distinct substrings.
Count paths from each state, then skip whole lexicographic groups when selecting k.
analogy: At each letter, a branch contains all substrings beginning with that choice; count the branch before deciding whether to enter it.
example: For aba the sorted distinct substrings are a, ab, aba, b, ba; k=3 gives aba.
algorithm: Build a suffix automaton. In decreasing state length compute ways[v]=sum over transitions v->u of (1+ways[u]), using wide integers. From the initial state examine transitions in character order; skip a branch if k exceeds 1+ways[u], otherwise append its character, decrement k for the substring ending there, and continue until k=0.
correctness: Every distinct substring labels exactly one path from the initial state. Each branch consists of its one-character extension followed by all longer paths, in lexicographic order, so subtracting branch sizes locates exactly the kth string.
complexity: For n characters over a fixed 26-letter alphabet, O(26n) time and O(26n) space.
